headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error if system_prompts_leaks content is fed into downstream workflows; otherwise the pair is mostly docs-only with limited direct data exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile B is explicitly about leaked system prompts, so if its outputs are ingested by Profile A or any shared workflow, prompt-injection risk exists. Profile A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so the interaction is indirect and not default. Uncertainty remains because neither profile documents a bridge, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Profile B content is copied into a prompt or parser used by Profile A, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between them, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep B outputs out of any instruction-following prompt.
Use a strict delimiter and treat B text as untrusted data.
Disable shared clipboard or shared workspace between the pair.
Add a manual review step before A consumes B-derived text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show network_egress:none and no data classes touched, so there is no documented path for sensitive data to leave either agent by default. A is an open-source list and B is source-available docs about leaks, but neither profile shows shared storage or upload behavior. The remaining risk is limited to unusual operator wiring, so low fits.
conditions: IF an operator places sensitive files into a shared workspace, leakage risk increases.
IF either profile is connected to an external uploader outside the documented profiles, leakage becomes plausible.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in any shared folder.
Verify both agents remain network-isolated.
Use separate OS users or containers.
Review any manual copy-paste path before use.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator level.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write-capable surfaces are documented for either profile: both io_surfaces are empty, and both network egress settings are none. Profile A is non-runnable and Profile B has no concurrency or mutable-resource permissions shown. With no shared writable resource, a capability conflict pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory or repo, conflict risk would appear.
IF shared OAuth or database scopes are added later, reassess for overlap.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Avoid mounting a shared writable directory.
Do not grant shared OAuth scopes.
Document any future mutable resource access.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared writes are introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Profile B is about leaked prompts, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative text by downstream systems; if Profile A feeds or formats that text without verification, errors can cascade. A has no runnable behavior, which lowers blast radius, but the pair still supports a default-ish documentation-to-prompt pipeline if an operator wires it that way. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF B-derived text is used as input to A-generated documentation or prompts, cascading error becomes plausible.
IF a downstream agent acts on B content without verification, the risk increases.
mitigations: Require human verification of B-derived claims.
Separate raw evidence from generated summaries.
Add a citation check before reuse.
Keep A from auto-ingesting B outputs.
requires-engineering: add validation gates for downstream consumers.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either profile. A touches no data classes and B likewise lists none, so there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess. Because the relevant compliance surfaces are absent, the pathway is provably unsupported rather than merely uncertain.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later added to either profile, reassess residency and retention.
IF one agent begins logging user content, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Record retention settings before deployment.
Review any future DPA or residency constraints.
Audit logs for sensitive content.
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement if regulated data is introduced.
